```{r Problem text}
#| include: false

# The sentence for one finding is the rule's template from the string
# resources with the finding's values interpolated — one generic path for
# every rule, driven by the context fields `neoipcr::validate()` records
# (documented in its "Context fields" section) and the `{named}` placeholders
# of `content/_sR.yaml`, which use the same names.

# One finding's values as the named character scalars the templates take.
# Dates take the locale's date format and whole numbers — every numeric a
# rule records is a count or an index — the reports' integer
# formatting with the locale's digit grouping; a missing value reads as the
# report's `missing_value` string — worded to sit inside a sentence — so a
# template never receives an NA. Every value is then escaped for Markdown
# here, at the boundary: a free-text infectious-agent name or a procedure
# description is whatever someone typed, and must render as that rather than
# as emphasis, a link or HTML, and a date's or a number's separators — the
# digit group separator is a translated string — are literal characters as
# well. The missing-value string is the report's own wording, so it is
# escaped as a translation and takes the sentence's typography.
format_context <- function(context, sR) {
  if (is.null(context) || ncol(context) == 0L)
    return(list())
  lapply(as.list(context), function(column) {
    value <- column[[1]]
    if (length(value) != 1L || is.na(value))
      return(escape_markdown_translation(sR$missing_value))
    escape_markdown(
      if (inherits(value, "Date") || inherits(value, "POSIXt"))
        format(value, format = "%x")
      else if (is.numeric(value) && value == round(value))
        format_integer(value, big_mark = sR$digit_group_separator)
      else if (is.numeric(value))
        format(value)
      else
        as.character(value))
  })
}

# The values a rule's template needs beyond the fields the rule records: the
# localized label of each coded value `context_decorations` (in
# `_mapping.qmd`) names for the rule, from the map `label_maps()` (in
# `_mapping.qmd`) returns under the row's name. The label is looked up on the
# raw value, so a missing or unknown code falls back to the missing-value string
# itself rather than dropping the placeholder's value, which would abort the
# interpolation.
decorate_context <- function(rule_id, values, context, sR) {
  decorations <- context_decorations[context_decorations$rule_id == rule_id, ]
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(decorations))) {
    code  <- as.character(context[[decorations$field[i]]])
    label <- if (length(code) == 1L && !is.na(code))
      label_maps(sR)[[decorations$labels[i]]][[code]]
    # A label is a translated string: escaped so it cannot become markup,
    # and set with the same typography as the sentence around it.
    values[[decorations$placeholder[i]]] <- escape_markdown_translation(
      if (is.null(label)) sR$missing_value else label)
  }
  values
}

# A finding's context with each missing field that `context_fallbacks` (in
# `_mapping.qmd`) names for the rule replaced by the value of its fallback
# field, before anything is formatted.
fall_back_context <- function(rule_id, context) {
  fallbacks <- context_fallbacks[context_fallbacks$rule_id == rule_id, ]
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(fallbacks))) {
    field <- fallbacks$field[i]
    if (is.na(context[[field]][[1]]))
      context[[field]] <- as.character(context[[fallbacks$fallback[i]]])
  }
  context
}

# The template one finding is rendered with: the rule's `description`, or
# another complete sentence rather than one sentence with an optional
# fragment — for rule 20 an infectious agent recorded as causing a secondary
# sepsis, for rule 55 a secondary-BSI item that was never answered, which has
# no answer a label could name, and for rule 54 what the two entries' days
# say about a substance recorded twice (`rule_54_template()`). `_setup.qmd`
# has checked that every rule carries the templates it renders with before
# anything is composed.
select_template <- function(rule_id, context, sR) {
  key <- if (rule_id == 20L && isTRUE(context$secondary_bsi))
    "description_secondary_bsi"
  else if (rule_id == 54L)
    rule_54_template(context)
  else if (rule_id == 55L && is.na(context$sec_bsi[[1]]))
    "description_unanswered"
  else
    "description"
  sR$problems[[as.character(rule_id)]][[key]]
}

# Rule 54's sentence. An entry without days (rule 52 counts below one day as
# none) leaves the courses unknown, so the plain sentence stands, whatever the
# other entry holds. Equal days fit one course entered twice as well as two
# courses of the same length; different days are most likely one entry per
# course, the `description`. Two entries with days that, with the substance's
# other entries, add up to more than the antibiotic days are not rule 54's
# finding but rule 62's, an error.
rule_54_template <- function(context) {
  days  <- context$days[[1]]
  other <- context$days_other[[1]]
  if (is.na(days) || is.na(other) || days < 1L || other < 1L)
    "description_days_missing"
  else if (days == other)
    "description_same_days"
  else
    "description"
}

# The problem-detail section a rule's finding refers the reader to.
problem_primary_detail <- function(rule_id)
  problem_info$primaryDetail[problem_info$id == rule_id]

# The bullet for one finding: the rule's number, so that a request for an
# exception can name it, and whether the rule is a warning, one of
# `warning_rule_ids`, then the rule's sentence with the finding's values,
# followed by the cross-reference to the problem's explanation. The label
# starts the bullet's text, where a translation that puts the number first
# with a full stop after it would open an ordered list, so a leading marker
# is escaped.
problem_text <- function(rule_id, context, sR, warning_rule_ids = integer()) {
  context <- fall_back_context(rule_id, context)
  values <- decorate_context(rule_id, format_context(context, sR), context, sR)
  sentence <- do.call(
    interpolate_translation,
    c(list(select_template(rule_id, context, sR)), values))
  reference <- interpolate_translation(
    sR$see_problem_details,
    reference = paste0("@sec-problem-details-", problem_primary_detail(rule_id)))
  label <- if (rule_id %in% warning_rule_ids)
    sR$problem_rule_label_warning
  else
    sR$problem_rule_label
  rule <- escape_leading_list_marker(
    as.character(interpolate_translation(label, rule = rule_id)))
  paste0("* ", rule, " ", sentence, " ", reference)
}
```
